doc: PROFILE.md 5.1, normative entry for this step's spatial-reference change: 'PROJJSON in SRS metadata -- `pdal info --metadata` grows a `srs.json` member carrying the PROJJSON description of the file's coordinate system. At this release it is an escaped JSON string; it becomes a nested object later.' -- the new member is an ADDITION, not a replacement. Measured on the real anchors with this fixture: at 2.4.0 `metadata.srs` has ten keys and no `json`; at 2.5.0 it has eleven, the new one being `json`, and `wkt` and `proj4` are still there beside it with the same values (`wkt` still opens with PROJCS["NAD83 / UTM zone 17N" and still closes on the EPSG 26917 authority at both anchors). The `exists` check on `metadata.srs.json` is what makes the case move: the three surviving-member assertions hold at both anchors by design -- they are what 'the other members remain' means -- so without it the case would pass at 2.4.0 as well. The `wkt` member is asserted by what it SAYS -- the CRS name at the front and the EPSG authority at the back -- and not by its character count. An exact length is a GDAL/PROJ serialization artefact: it is byte-identical at 2.4.0 and 2.5.0, so it discriminates nothing, and it can only ever fail for a reason that has nothing to do with this step.
